title.zh: 卷八十一 列傳第十一: 耶律室魯 王繼忠 蕭孝忠 陳昭袞 蕭合卓
title.en: Volume 81 Biographies 11: Yelu Shilu, Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, Xiao Hezhuo
title.raw: 卷八十一 列傳第十一: 耶律室魯 王繼忠 蕭孝忠 陳昭袞 蕭合卓 Volume 81 Biographies 11: Yelu Shilu, Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, Xiao Hezhuo

sentences.zh: 耶律室魯

translations.literal: Yelü Shilu
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shilu

sentences.zh: 〈（歐裏斯）〉

translations.literal: (Orris)
translations.idiomatic: (Orris)

sentences.zh: 王繼忠蕭孝忠陳昭袞蕭合卓

translations.literal: Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, Xiao Hezhuo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhong, Xiao Xiaozhong, Chen Zhaogun, and Xiao Hezhuo

sentences.zh: 耶律室魯，字乙辛隱，六院部人。

translations.literal: Yelü Shilu, style name Yixin Yin, was a man of the Six Courts tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Shilu, whose style was Yixin Yin, came from the Six Courts tribe.

sentences.zh: 魁岸美容儀。

translations.literal: He was imposing in stature and handsome in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and striking, with a handsome presence.

sentences.zh: 聖宗同年生，帝愛之。

translations.literal: He was born in the same year as Emperor Shengzong; the emperor loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the same year as Emperor Shengzong, he won the emperor's affection.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: Upon first putting on the cap, he was appointed attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he came of age, he was made an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為宿直官。

translations.literal: Before long he became a night-duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was assigned to night duty at court.

sentences.zh: 及出師伐宋，為隊帥，從南府宰相耶律奴瓜、統軍使蕭撻覽略地趙、魏，有功，加檢校太師，為北院大王。

translations.literal: When the army marched out to attack Song, he served as column commander, following the Southern Chancellery Chancellor Yelü Nugua and the army commander Xiao Talan in seizing territory in Zhao and Wei; for his merit he was made acting Grand Preceptor and Northern Chancellery Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were sent against Song, he served as column commander under the Southern Chancellery chancellor Yelü Nugua and the army commander Xiao Talan, helping seize territory in Zhao and Wei. For this service he was promoted to acting grand preceptor and made grandee of the Northern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 攻拔通利軍。

translations.literal: He stormed and took Tongli Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Tongli Circuit.

sentences.zh: 宋和議成，特進門下平章事，賜推誠竭節保義功臣。

translations.literal: When the Song peace treaty was concluded, he was made specially advanced grand councilor of the Secretariat and granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Steadfast Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After peace with Song was concluded, he was made specially advanced grand councilor of the Secretariat and granted the title Meritorious Subject of Sincere Devotion and Steadfast Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 以本部俸羊多闕，部人空乏，請以羸老之羊及皮毛歲易南中絹，彼此利之。

translations.literal: Because stipend sheep for his tribe were often lacking and his tribesmen were impoverished, he requested to exchange each year lean old sheep and hides for silk from the south, to the mutual benefit of both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Because stipend sheep for his tribe were chronically short and his tribesmen were impoverished, he asked to trade each year old or weak sheep and hides for southern silk, to the benefit of both sides.

sentences.zh: 拜北院樞密使，封韓王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Northern Chancellery commissioner and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner of the Northern Chancellery and enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 自韓德讓知北院，職多廢曠，室魯拜命之日，朝野相慶。

translations.literal: Since Han Derang had overseen the Northern Chancellery, many duties had fallen into neglect; on the day Shilu received his appointment, court and countryside alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Han Derang had overseen the Northern Chancellery, many of its duties had lapsed; when Shilu took office, the court and the realm rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 從上獵松林，至沙嶺卒，年四十四，贈守司徒、政事令。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a hunt in Songlin, he died at Shaling, aged forty-four; posthumously he was given the offices of acting Minister over the Masses and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor on a hunt in Songlin, he died at Shaling at the age of forty-four and was posthumously granted the ranks of acting minister over the masses and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二子：十神奴、歐裏斯。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Shishennu and Orris.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shishennu and Orris.

sentences.zh: 十神奴，南院大王。

translations.literal: Shishennu became Southern Chancellery Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Shishennu rose to grandee of the Southern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 歐裏思，字留隱，少有大志。

translations.literal: Orris, style name Liuyin, from youth had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Orris, whose style was Liuyin, had shown great ambition from youth.

sentences.zh: 未冠，補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: Before he had put on the cap, he was appointed attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age, he was made an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 開泰初，為本部司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kai Tai era, he became tribal minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kai Tai era, he became minister of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 秩滿閑居，徵為郎君班詳穩。

translations.literal: When his term ended he lived in retirement; he was summoned to be overseer of the attendant gentlemen corps.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he retired to private life, then was recalled as overseer of the attendant gentlemen corps.

sentences.zh: 遷右皮室詳穩，將本部兵，從東平王蕭排押伐高麗，至茶、陀二河，戰不利。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be overseer of the Right Pishi Guard, leading his tribal troops to follow the Prince of Dongping, Xiao Paiya, in attacking Goryeo; at the Cha and Tuo rivers the fighting went badly.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to overseer of the Right Pishi Guard and led his tribal forces with the Prince of Dongping, Xiao Paiya, against Goryeo; at the Cha and Tuo rivers the campaign went badly.

sentences.zh: 歐裏斯獨全軍還，帝嘉賞。

translations.literal: Orris alone brought the army back intact; the emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Orris alone brought his force back intact, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 終西南面招討使。

translations.literal: He ended his career as commissioner for punitive campaigns in the Southwest.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as commissioner for punitive campaigns in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 王繼忠，不知何郡人。

translations.literal: Wang Jizhong—it is not known from which commandery he came.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhong was a man of unknown native commandery.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為鄆州刺史、殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: He served Song as prefect of Yanzhou and chief adjutant of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: In Song service he held the posts of prefect of Yanzhou and chief adjutant of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 統和二十一年，宋遣繼忠屯定之望都，以輕騎覘我軍，遇南府宰相耶律奴瓜等，獲之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Tonghe, Song sent Jizhong to garrison Wangdu in Dingzhou; with light cavalry he reconnoitered our army, encountered the Southern Chancellery Chancellor Yelü Nugua and others, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Tonghe, Song posted Jizhong at Wangdu in Ding prefecture; he led light cavalry to scout our forces, met the Southern Chancellery chancellor Yelü Nugua and others, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太后知其賢，授戶部使，以康默記族女女之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager knew him to be worthy and appointed him commissioner of the Household Bureau; she gave him a daughter of the Kang Mojiji clan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing his talent, the empress dowager made him commissioner of the household bureau and gave him a daughter of the Kang Mojiji clan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 繼忠亦自激昂，事必盡力。

translations.literal: Jizhong too roused himself in spirit and in every matter gave his utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong likewise threw himself into his duties and spared no effort in whatever he undertook.

sentences.zh: 宋以繼忠先朝舊臣，每遣使，必有附賜，聖宗許受之。

translations.literal: Because Song regarded Jizhong as a former minister of the previous reign, whenever it sent envoys there were always attached gifts for him; Emperor Shengzong permitted him to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Song treated Jizhong as a former minister of the prior dynasty and, whenever it sent envoys, always included gifts for him; Emperor Shengzong allowed him to accept them.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，宋使來聘，遺繼忠弧矢、鞭策及求和劄子，有曰：「自臨大位，愛養黎元。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, a Song envoy came on a mission of courtesy and sent Jizhong a bow and arrows, a riding crop, and a memorial seeking peace, which read: "Since I assumed the great throne, I have cherished and nurtured the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year a Song envoy arrived on a diplomatic mission and sent Jizhong a bow and arrows, a riding crop, and a memorial seeking peace, which read: "Since I took the throne, I have cherished and nurtured the people.

sentences.zh: 豈欲窮兵，惟思息戰。

translations.literal: How could I wish to exhaust the realm in war? I think only of ceasing hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: I have no wish to exhaust the realm in war; I think only of ending the fighting.

sentences.zh: 每敕邊事，嚴諭守臣。

translations.literal: Whenever I issue orders on border affairs, I sternly instruct the frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I issue orders on border affairs, I sternly instruct the frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 至於北界人民，不令小有侵擾，眾所具悉，爾亦備知。

translations.literal: As for the people of the northern border, I do not allow even slight harassment; all know this fully, and you too are well aware of it.
translations.idiomatic: As for the people on the northern frontier, I allow no harassment, however slight; everyone knows this, and you are fully aware of it as well.

sentences.zh: 向以知雄州何承矩已布此懇，自後杳無所聞。

translations.literal: Earlier I learned that He Chengju of Xiongzhou had already conveyed this plea; since then I have heard nothing further.
translations.idiomatic: I had understood that He Chengju of Xiong prefecture had already conveyed this plea; since then I have heard nothing more.

sentences.zh: 汝可密言，如許通和，即當別使往請。」

translations.literal: You may speak to them in secret: if they agree to peace, I shall at once send another envoy to request it."
translations.idiomatic: You may tell them privately that if they agree to peace, I shall immediately send another envoy to request it."

sentences.zh: 詔繼忠與宋使相見，仍許講和。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jizhong to meet the Song envoy and peace negotiations were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Jizhong to meet the Song envoy and authorized peace talks.

sentences.zh: 以繼忠家無奴隸，賜宮戶三十，加左武衛上將軍，攝中京留守。

translations.literal: Because Jizhong's household had no slaves, thirty palace households were granted him; he was made left martial guard general and acting defender of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jizhong's household had no servants, he was granted thirty palace households; he was promoted to left martial guard general and made acting defender of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 開泰五年，為漢人行宮都部署，封瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kai Tai he became overall commander of the Han Chinese palace encampment and was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kai Tai he was made overall commander of the Han palace encampment and enfeoffed as prince of Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 六年，進楚王，賜國姓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and granted the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was advanced to Prince of Chu and granted the imperial clan surname.

sentences.zh: 上嘗燕飲，議以蕭合卓為北院樞密使，繼忠曰：「合卓雖有刀筆才，暗於大體。

translations.literal: Once at a banquet the emperor discussed appointing Xiao Hezhuo Northern Chancellery commissioner; Jizhong said: "Although Hezhuo has clerical talent, he is blind to the larger picture.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor once discussed appointing Xiao Hezhuo commissioner of the Northern Chancellery; Jizhong said, "Hezhuo may have a gift for paperwork, but he lacks grasp of the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 蕭敵烈才行兼備，可任。」

translations.literal: Xiao Dilie has both talent and conduct and can fill the post."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Dilie has both talent and character and would be fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 上不納，竟用合卓。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this and in the end employed Hezhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him and in the end appointed Hezhuo.

sentences.zh: 及遣合卓伐高麗，繼忠為行軍副部署，攻興化鎮，月餘不下。

translations.literal: When Hezhuo was sent to attack Goryeo, Jizhong served as deputy campaign commander; they besieged Xinghua garrison for more than a month without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhuo was dispatched against Goryeo, Jizhong served as deputy campaign commander; they attacked Xinghua garrison for more than a month without capturing it.

sentences.zh: 師還，上謂明於知人，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor said he was clear-sighted in judging men and appointed him commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, the emperor declared that he had shown sound judgment of men and appointed him commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平三年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 子懷玉，仕至防禦使。

translations.literal: His son Huaiyu rose in service to defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaiyu rose in service to the rank of defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蕭孝忠，字撒板，小字圖古斯，誌慷慨。

translations.literal: Xiao Xiaozhong, style name Saban, childhood name Tugusi, was noted for bold generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xiaozhong, whose style was Saban and childhood name Tugusi, was known for bold generosity.

sentences.zh: 開泰中，補祗候郎君，尚越國公主，拜駙馬都尉，累遷殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: During Kai Tai he was appointed attendant gentleman, married Princess Yueguo, was made commissioner of the imperial son-in-law, and was repeatedly promoted to chief inspector of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kai Tai era he was made an attendant gentleman, married Princess Yueguo, was appointed commissioner of the imperial son-in-law, and rose to chief inspector of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 太平中，擢北府宰相。

translations.literal: During Taiping he was promoted to Northern Prefecture chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping era he was promoted to chancellor of the Northern Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 重熙七年，為東京留守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongxi he became defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chongxi he was made defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時禁渤海人擊球，孝忠言：「東京最為重鎮，無從禽之地，若非球馬，何以習武？

translations.literal: At the time Bohai people were forbidden to play cuju. Xiaozhong said: "The Eastern Capital is the most important garrison; there is no place for hunting. If not for ball and horse, how can one practice martial arts?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bohai people were forbidden to play cuju. Xiaozhong said, "The Eastern Capital is the most important garrison, and there is no place for hunting. Without ball and horse, how can one train in martial arts?

sentences.zh: 且天子以四海為家，何分彼此？

translations.literal: Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home—why distinguish between us and them?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home—why distinguish between one and another?

sentences.zh: 宜弛其禁。」

translations.literal: The prohibition should be relaxed."
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition should be relaxed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入朝，封楚王，拜北院樞密使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he came to court, was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu, and appointed Northern Chancellery commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he came to court, was enfeoffed as Prince of Chu, and appointed commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 國制，以契丹、漢人分北、南院樞密治之，孝忠奏曰：「一國二樞密，風俗所以不同。

translations.literal: Under the state system, Khitan and Han were divided and governed by separate Northern and Southern Chancellery commissioners. Xiaozhong memorialized: "One state with two commissioners is why customs differ.
translations.idiomatic: Under the state system, Khitan and Han were governed by separate Northern and Southern Chancellery commissioners. Xiaozhong memorialized, "One state with two commissioners is why customs differ.

sentences.zh: 若並為一，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: If they were merged into one, the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: If they were merged into one, the realm would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 事未及行，薨。

translations.literal: Before the matter could be carried out, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter could be carried out, he died.

sentences.zh: 追封楚國王。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 帝素服哭臨，赦死囚數人，為孝忠薦福。

translations.literal: The emperor wore plain mourning garb and came to weep; he pardoned several condemned prisoners as a merit-offering for Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore plain mourning garb and came to weep; he pardoned several condemned prisoners to accumulate merit for Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 葬日，親臨，賜宮戶守冢。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the emperor came in person and granted palace households to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the emperor came in person and granted palace households to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: 子阿速，終南院樞密使。

translations.literal: His son Asu ended his career as Southern Chancellery commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Asu ended his career as commissioner of the Southern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 陳昭袞，小字王九，雲州人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhaogun, childhood name Wang Jiu, was a man of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhaogun, known in youth as Wang Jiu, was a native of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 工譯鞮，勇而善射。

translations.literal: He was skilled at translating the Khitan language, brave, and adept at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at Khitan interpretation, brave, and an excellent archer.

sentences.zh: 統和中，補祗候郎君，為奚拽剌詳穩，累遷敦睦宮太保，兼掌圍場事。

translations.literal: During Tonghe he was appointed attendant gentleman, became overseer of the Xi Zhuaila guard, and was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian of the Dunmu Palace, concurrently managing the hunting grounds.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era he was made an attendant gentleman, then overseer of the Xi Zhuaila guard, and was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian of Dunmu Palace while also overseeing the imperial hunting grounds.

sentences.zh: 開泰五年秋，大獵，帝射虎，以馬馳太速，矢不及發。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Kai Tai, during a great hunt, the emperor shot at a tiger; his horse galloped too fast and the arrow could not be loosed in time.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Kai Tai, during a grand hunt, the emperor charged a tiger; his horse ran too fast and he could not loose his arrow in time.

sentences.zh: 虎怒，奮勢將犯蹕。

translations.literal: The tiger grew enraged and, gathering its strength, was about to charge the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger, enraged, gathered itself to charge the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 左右辟易，昭袞舍馬，捉虎兩耳騎之。

translations.literal: Those at left and right scattered; Zhaogun abandoned his horse, seized the tiger by both ears, and mounted it.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the emperor scattered; Zhaogun leapt from his horse, seized the tiger by both ears, and rode astride it.

sentences.zh: 虎駭，且逸。

translations.literal: The tiger was terrified and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the tiger bolted.

sentences.zh: 上命衛士追射，昭袞大呼止之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the guards to pursue and shoot; Zhaogun shouted loudly for them to stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the guards to pursue and shoot, but Zhaogun shouted for them to stop.

sentences.zh: 虎雖軼山，昭袞終不墮地。

translations.literal: Though the tiger leapt over hills, Zhaogun in the end did not fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Though the tiger bounded over hill after hill, Zhaogun never fell.

sentences.zh: 伺便，拔佩刀殺之。

translations.literal: Watching for an opening, he drew his belt knife and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw his chance, he drew his belt knife and killed it.

sentences.zh: 輦至上前，慰勞良久。

translations.literal: When he came before the emperor in the imperial carriage, the emperor comforted and praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Brought before the emperor's carriage, he was comforted and praised at length.

sentences.zh: 即日設燕，悉以席上金銀器賜之，特加節鉞，遷圍場都太師，賜國姓，命張儉、呂德懋賦以美之。

translations.literal: That same day a banquet was held and all the gold and silver vessels on the table were bestowed on him; he was specially granted the command baton, promoted to grand master of the hunting grounds, granted the imperial surname, and Zhang Jian and Lü Demao were ordered to compose verses in his praise.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a banquet was held and every gold and silver vessel on the table was given to him; he was specially granted the command baton, promoted to grand master of the hunting grounds, granted the imperial clan surname, and Zhang Jian and Lü Demao were ordered to compose verses in his praise.

sentences.zh: 遷歸義軍節度使，同知上京留守，歷西南面招討都監，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Guiyi Army, associate defender of the Supreme Capital, and served successively as overall overseer of punitive campaigns in the Southwest; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Guiyi Army and associate defender of the Supreme Capital, later served as overall overseer of punitive campaigns in the southwest, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 蕭合卓，字合魯隱，突呂不部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Hezhuo, style name Helu Yin, was a man of the Tulübu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hezhuo, whose style was Helu Yin, came from the Tulübu tribe.

sentences.zh: 始為本部吏。

translations.literal: He began as a clerk of his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in his tribe.

sentences.zh: 統和初，以謹恪，補南院侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, for his careful diligence he was appointed Southern Chancellery vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tonghe era, his scrupulous diligence won him appointment as vice minister of the Southern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 十八年，北院樞密使韓德讓舉合卓為中丞，以太后遺物使宋。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Northern Chancellery Commissioner Han Derang recommended Hezhuo as chief censor and sent him as envoy to Song bearing the empress dowager's parting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the Northern Chancellery commissioner Han Derang recommended Hezhuo as chief censor and sent him to Song bearing the empress dowager's parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 還，遷北院樞密副使。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to deputy Northern Chancellery commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made deputy commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 開泰三年，為左夷離畢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kai Tai he became Left Yilibi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kai Tai he was made Left Yilibi.

sentences.zh: 合卓久居近職，明習典故，善占對。

translations.literal: Hezhuo had long held posts close to the throne, was well versed in precedent, and skilled at responsive discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhuo had long held posts close to the throne, was well versed in precedent, and excelled at court repartee.

sentences.zh: 以是尤被寵渥，升北院樞密使。

translations.literal: For this he was especially favored and promoted to Northern Chancellery commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was especially favored and promoted to commissioner of the Northern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時議以為無完行，不可大用；

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that he lacked integrity of conduct and could not be entrusted with great responsibility;
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that he lacked integrity and should not be entrusted with great responsibility;

sentences.zh: 南院樞密使王繼忠侍宴，又譏其短。

translations.literal: the Southern Chancellery Commissioner Wang Jizhong, attending a banquet, again mocked his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: at a banquet the Southern Chancellery commissioner Wang Jizhong again mocked his shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 帝頗不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣合卓伐高麗，還，時求進者多附之；

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hezhuo was sent to attack Goryeo; on his return, many who sought advancement attached themselves to him;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hezhuo was sent against Goryeo; on his return, many office-seekers flocked to him;

sentences.zh: 然其服食、仆馬不加於舊。

translations.literal: yet his food, drink, and servants and horses were no more than before.
translations.idiomatic: yet his food, clothing, servants, and horses were no more lavish than before.

sentences.zh: 帝知其廉，以族屬女妻其子，詔許親友饋獻，豪貴奔趨於門。

translations.literal: The emperor knew him to be incorrupt and gave him a clanswoman in marriage to his son; an edict permitted friends and kin to send gifts, and the powerful and wealthy rushed to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recognized his integrity, gave a clanswoman in marriage to his son, and issued an edict permitting friends and kin to send gifts; the powerful and wealthy thronged his gate.

sentences.zh: 太平五年，有疾，帝欲臨視，合卓辭曰：「臣無狀，猥蒙重任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping he fell ill; the emperor wished to visit him in person. Hezhuo declined, saying: "Your subject is without merit yet has presumptuously received a weighty post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping he fell ill; the emperor wished to visit him in person. Hezhuo declined, saying, "Your subject is without merit, yet I have presumptuously received a weighty post.

sentences.zh: 今形容毀瘁，恐陛下見而動心。」

translations.literal: Now my appearance is wasted and haggard; I fear that if Your Majesty sees me, it will stir your heart."
translations.idiomatic: My appearance is now wasted and haggard; I fear that if Your Majesty sees me, it will distress you."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 會北府宰相蕭樸問疾，合卓執其手曰：「吾死，君必為樞密使，慎勿舉勝己者。」

translations.literal: When the Northern Prefecture Chancellor Xiao Pu came to inquire after his illness, Hezhuo took his hand and said: "When I die, you are certain to become commissioner; be careful not to recommend anyone better than yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Prefecture chancellor Xiao Pu came to inquire after his illness, Hezhuo took his hand and said, "When I die, you are sure to become commissioner; be careful never to recommend anyone better than yourself."

sentences.zh: 樸出而鄙之。

translations.literal: Pu left and despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Pu left and despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 是日卒。

translations.literal: That same day he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he died.

sentences.zh: 子烏古，終本部節度使。

translations.literal: His son Wugu ended his career as tribal military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wugu ended his career as military commissioner of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 論曰：統和諸臣，名昭王室者多矣。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Among the ministers of the Tonghe era, many were famed for making the royal house illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Among the ministers of the Tonghe era, many won renown for bringing glory to the royal house.

sentences.zh: 室魯拜樞密使，朝野相慶，必有得民心者。

translations.literal: When Shilu was appointed commissioner, court and countryside rejoiced together—he must surely have won the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilu was appointed commissioner, court and countryside rejoiced together; he must surely have won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 繼忠既不能死國，雖通南北之和，有知人之鑒，奚足尚哉！

translations.literal: Jizhong, having failed to die for his state, though he brought peace between north and south and had discernment in judging men—what is there to esteem!
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong, having failed to die for his state, may have brokered peace between north and south and shown discernment in judging men, but what is there to esteem in that!

sentences.zh: 孝忠、昭袞，皆有可稱者。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong and Zhaogun each had qualities worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong and Zhaogun each had qualities worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 合卓臨終，教蕭樸毋舉勝己者任樞密，其誤國之罪大矣！

translations.literal: Hezhuo on his deathbed instructed Xiao Pu never to recommend anyone better than himself for the commissionership—the crime of misleading the state was grave indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Hezhuo on his deathbed instructed Xiao Pu never to recommend anyone better than himself for the commissionership—a crime against the state of the gravest kind!
